phase: Phase 4b: The live runs and the first track A results (by Sun 2026-11-22)
summary: Pass under the PM round cap. Three implementation defects remain nonblocking. The new test file passes with skipped defect pins. No real-key leak into a committed file or public page was reproduced.
nonblocking_findings: ADV-P4D-1 [Nit] adversarial-testing: The seed reason patterns accept trailing credential text. Both full runner probes printed the appended synthetic value and exited 2. See review-run.sh:813-816, judge-run.sh:576-579, and adversarial-p4d.test.ts:216. The current helper emits fixed text, so this proves a dependency-boundary gap, not a real-key leak. Route to Green: emit fixed text for an exact provider-specific reason. This confirms the earlier Review B seed-reason finding.

ADV-P4D-2 [Nit] adversarial-testing: The 499-byte cut can split a UTF-8 code point. Both error_line_of probes emitted invalid UTF-8 for 498 ASCII bytes followed by an emoji. Decoding expanded the 500 output bytes to 502 bytes. The full judge path stored and printed the replacement character. See review-run.sh:964, judge-run.sh:729, and adversarial-p4d.test.ts:260. Route to Green: preserve the byte limit and a complete UTF-8 code point.

ADV-P4D-3 [Nit] adversarial-testing: A truncated final step_finish event leaves tokens_complete true after an earlier valid event. Both readers returned 5,0,0,0,0,1. See review-run.sh:163, judge-run.sh:121, and adversarial-p4d.test.ts:267. This confirms Review A F8 and Review B N27 cut tail. Route to Green: clear completeness when the final token event is truncated.

New coverage: adversarial-p4d.test.ts passes 21 cases and skips six defect pins. Each of the three findings has one skipped pin per runner. E1 in adversarial-p4c.test.ts remains active and passes. No skip hides a previously active failure.

Seed boundary: both runner CLIs preserve the exact no-entry reason and drop an unexpected helper error containing a synthetic value. Each exits 2, makes no model call, and prints only the expected refusal plus the cleanup diagnostic. Appending the same synthetic value to the allowed prefix bypasses that suppression in both CLIs.

Error scan: actual scan_output and error_line_of functions redact a value split across three supported error shapes. They also redact a JSON-escaped value across the cut edge. A helper that prints the value on stderr and fails yields only the distinct fixed scan text. The full judge path writes one open record with that fixed text and no synthetic value.

UTF-8 proof: both actual functions emit 500 bytes including the newline for 498 ASCII bytes followed by an emoji. The bytes fail the UTF-8 round-trip assertion. The decoded output has 502 bytes. The full judge CLI exits 0 with state open and writes the replacement character into its error record.

Token proof: both readers retain the exact sum 2^53-1 with flag 1 and clear the flag at 2^53. Removing the accumulated-sum check in memory changes the latter flag to 1. A valid event followed by a truncated step_finish still returns flag 1.

Marker proof: both daemon_pids functions select only the exact local job marker. The foreign entries share HOME, cwd, and argv. A prefix-sharing job root and a marker with trailing text remain excluded. No live foreign process was needed for this synthetic proc-table test.

XDG proof: each runner guard refuses a dangling symlink under every call folder at depths 0, 1, 2, and 4. Each refusal has exit 2 and the exact folder reason. Both guards accept a clean nested tree. The judge block executes inside a function, as production requires.

Decoder proof: the full judge CLI selects the final text block across several text events. Forged result events before and after that text cannot change the verdict. The queue CLI joins several text parts and preserves the exact expected claim. Fresh decode-parity coverage passes all three public readers.

Mutation proof: removing the joined-event scan in memory changes the three-shape result from the fixed text to a credential fragment. The new assertion rejects that result. Removing the sum check changes the unsafe-sum completeness flag. Both mutations reproduce in both runner copies without a production edit.

A4: the actual framework phase_counts function received an all-[~] fixture plan. It returned total=2, complete=0, in_progress=2, incomplete=2. No markers-consistent command exists in the implementation scope. The fixture does not appear complete.

A7: both actual scans preserve a credential hit when the synthetic value starts with never and the error line includes do not. They return the exact fixed credential text. No English-word filter removes the hit.

A5: the selected plan has no all checks pass or PASS=N, FAIL=0 claim. The fresh E1, decoder, runner-boundary, and earlier adversarial commands exit 0. This audit makes no full-suite or live-phase acceptance claim.

Hermeticity: the final new-file run also passed with BENCH_TRACK=change, MG_SCAN_FAIL=1, and BENCH_RA_QUOTA=/nonexistent inherited. The fixture environment uses an allowlist. It pins HOME, XDG paths, TMPDIR, TZ, fake paths, and the quota stub. No model or real quota source runs.

Fixture corrections: the first draft had eight assertion or extraction failures. I corrected cleanup-output expectations, the HOME reason, function scope, and the missing daemon-output newline. The next normal run passed. The final hostile-environment run also passed. An exploratory bun eval initially rejected afterEach outside a test runner; the corrected probe removed only that registration.

Safety: a credential-pattern search over the exact production diff returned zero hits. bash -n and git diff --check passed. Public pages and frozen paths have empty diffs. Final pgrep found no matching fake or quota server. The test afterEach also checks recorded fake PIDs before removing each temp tree.

Limits: I read no real credential store, private key, seeded diff, raw model output, or adjudication note. I ran no model, browser, opencode CLI, or openchamber CLI. Synthetic values reached temporary files only. I did not repeat the private-data leak gate. No real-key leak into a committed file or public page was observed.

Disposition: no CONTEST item was supplied. The PM cap keeps all findings nonblocking. The pass status reflects that cap, not the absence of defects. Green owns their remediation. Any later implementation commit requires a fresh adversarial run. Facts changed: none.
